key_insight: CaseScope exposes unstable case-level pathology diagnosis in multimodal LLMs: the best open and proprietary models answered correctly across all ten option rotations on just 17.9% and 61.7% of teaching cases, respectively.
clinical_relevance: The benchmark tests integration of multiple pathology fields, highlighting reliability gaps relevant to evaluating potential diagnostic support tools.
method: Combined 436 residency-teaching cases with 800 cases from 88 published pathology atlases.
Evaluated six tasks spanning diagnosis, morphological finding verification, and finding localization.
Tested 28 open and four proprietary multimodal LLMs, including sensitivity to answer-option order.
evidence_signal: Across 4,679 items covering 843 entities and 18 organ systems, most open models verified findings only modestly above chance, while model rankings broadly replicated across the two sources.
watch_item: Curated teaching and atlas fields, including atlas labels derived through agreement between two LLMs, do not establish performance in prospective clinical workflows.
paper_title: CaseScope: A Multi-Field Benchmark for Case-Level Pathology Diagnosis with Multimodal LLMs
